lines.en: My body grows abruptly heavy as I feel water flood my lungs. A lurching sensation of being sucked somewhere. I timed my fall, so I won't be torn apart and eaten. But I mustn't lose consciousness here.
I have to stay conscious.
I just have to hold on a little longer.
Somehow, I kept my body curled up and held my breath. 10 seconds, 20 seconds, 30······ I finally managed to draw breath when my hand touched a soft wall in the darkness.
“U-urgh.”
Only after vomiting up river water several times did I manage to catch my breath.
Thanks to my level 10 Constitution, I had at least survived the impact with the water, but the bruises scattered all over my body, large and small, stung badly.
Controlling my breathing to keep myself from panicking, I fumbled inside my clothes and turned on my smartphone.
I had worried the fall might have broken it, but fortunately, it still powered on. Thank goodness I had splurged on a waterproof smartphone.
Flash.
As the flashlight came on, my surroundings emerged dimly into view.
The broad expanse of stomach wall and chunks of concrete debris floating about.
The ichthyosaur's stomach was even more disgusting than I had imagined.
“Goddamn it.”

I vividly remembered Yoo Joonghyuk's expression as he released his grip without hesitation and left the bridge. I had expected it, but actually having it happen to me was more of a shock than I had anticipated.
······He was probably telling me that if I wanted to be his companion, I should be able to survive at least this much.
It wasn't as though I couldn't understand.
Companion. For Yoo Joonghyuk, of all people, that word carried that much weight. Ever since his first regression round ended in failure, Yoo Joonghyuk had never made a true ‘companion.’
Few humans could easily keep pace with his growth as a regressor. So he solved everything alone and was revered as a savior, and naturally, he grew lonely.
To Yoo Joonghyuk, ‘humans’ were either subordinates or enemies.
So this was a test.
A test telling me that if I wanted to stand as his equal, I should be able to handle at least this much alone.
······That was how it looked strictly from Yoo Joonghyuk's perspective, anyway.
“Companion, my ass······ You fucking psychopath.”
I dog-paddled over and barely managed to haul myself onto a floating Styrofoam panel.
The stomach's heat had eased the cold considerably, but the real problem began now.
Closing my eyes, I replayed the message log I had heard during my fall.
[You have failed to clear the scenario.]
[Paid settlement will now begin.]
[100 coins have been deducted as a channel fee.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ nods at your bold declaration.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ nods at your choice.]
[You have received a donation of 100 coins.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is disappointed by your rash declaration.]
Quite a few messages had arrived. The donations from constellations who had revealed their modifiers to me were particularly noticeable.
Probably because of my last conversation with Yoo Joonghyuk.
As I read the constellations' messages one by one and collected the coins, I felt a little wistful.
If I had chosen one of these guys during the first <Sponsor Selection>, I might never have ended up in this situation.
But I didn't regret my choice.
Having faced Yoo Joonghyuk myself, I knew for certain now.

The Great Sage, Heaven's Equal was a top-tier constellation sponsor, but he alone still wouldn't be enough. To stand against Yoo Joonghyuk, I needed something more than a mere ‘constellation sponsor.’
And here, I would obtain it.
Splash.
The stomach walls heaved, sending small waves through the ichthyosaur's insides.
The Sea-Commander seemed to be moving somewhere. I turned on my smartphone and calculated the time.
According to ‘Ways of Survival,’ ichthyosaurs began secreting stomach acid roughly 3 hours after feeding.
In other words, I didn't have much time left.
[Haha, what a shame. Things were getting so exciting.]
A voice came from the air, accompanied by a crackling sound effect.
“······Dokkaebi?”
[Yes, that's right. You're not surprised at all, are you?]
“I knew you'd come.”
[Hmm. You make it sound as though you've been waiting for me.]
“I have, of course.”
A light flashed in the air, and the dokkaebi appeared. His expression alone didn't tell me exactly what he was thinking, but his interest was plain.
I deliberately continued in a calm voice. If I let him overwhelm me right from the start, I would get nowhere.
“You have some coins to collect from me, don't you?”
“I failed the scenario, so you need to collect coins as payment.”
[Hmm, rather than your life?]
“If you were going to take my life, you would have put ‘Death’ in the failure penalty field instead of three question marks. Doesn't that mean there's room to negotiate?
[······Hahaha. Interesting.]
In truth, there was a hole in my argument.
The phrase ‘Failure: ???’ in the scenario message literally meant that the penalty for failure was unknown.
The idea that he would demand coins as payment was nothing more than a wild guess.
And yet, the reason I could be so certain.
“Am I wrong?”
Was that I already knew about the scenario.
After a moment's hesitation, the dokkaebi nodded.
[You're right. Remarkable. To deduce that much from such a small clue······ No wonder you're an incarnation who's caught the constellations' attention.]
The dokkaebi sounded sincerely impressed.
[As you said, even if you fail a sub-scenario, you can survive as long as you can pay the coins.]
“How much?”
[Pay 5100 coins. Then I'll at least let you keep your life.]
I checked my current coin balance.
[Coins held: 5100 C]
I let out a snort.
This bastard was trying to fleece me.
“That's too much.”
[Haha, then why don't you fucking die? Accepting coins is entirely at my discretion. If you piss me off, I could just end things right here, you know?]
“Then go ahead and kill me.”
[······Pardon?]
“I said, kill me.”
“You can't, can you?”
The dokkaebi didn't move. Of course he didn't.
He was making a tidy profit off me right now. Besides, if he had intended to kill me, he would never have come all the way down here to see me in the first place.
There was a reason he needed me to survive this, or at least die miserably.
[Haha. This is really pissing me off. Listen, right now, you and me······.]
The dokkaebi's straight eyebrows twitched violently. Time to stop provoking him and get to the point.
“Low-ranking dokkaebi Bihyung (鼻荊). How's life as a storyteller (Streamer) treating you?”
If an expression could crack, it would look exactly like that. For the first time, bewilderment spread across the dokkaebi Bihyung's face.
[H-how do you know my name?]
“Broadcasting hasn't felt very rewarding lately, has it? The constellations are awfully stingy, too.”
[W-what are you? How could a mere human know that······.]
Bihyung's trembling horn.
Understandable.
There was no way an ordinary human would know about the Star Stream (Star stream) system.
But I wasn't an ordinary human.
[A few constellations harbor doubts about your existence.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ has a gleam in its eyes at your plan.]
It wouldn't do for the constellations to hear what came next. I mouthed my words to Bihyung.
“How about closing the channel for a moment so we can talk?”
After some deliberation, Bihyung closed the channel.
[Channel #BI-7623 has closed.]
Once the constellations left the channel, Bihyung showed his true colors, too.
[Now, explain yourself. How does an ordinary human like you know about Star Stream broadcasting (星流放送)?]
“That isn't what matters.”
[Pardon?]
“Bihyung, don't you want to become the ‘Dokkaebi King’?”
[What are you―]
“I'm asking whether you want to surpass Dokgak (獨脚) and Gildal (吉達) and become the greatest storyteller among all the spirits and monsters (魑魅魍魎).”
Bihyung's complexion was changing.
“Dokkaebi Bihyung, make a contract with me. Then I'll make you the king of the dokkaebis.”
The Star Stream system.
Also called Star Stream (星流) broadcasting, this system was, simply put, a broadcasting operation for the entire universe.
The subscribers were the constellations at the pinnacle of those distant galaxies.
The actors were humans like me.
And the storyteller connecting the two was the dokkaebi right before my eyes.
[Ha, hahahahaha! You're insane! An insane human! I should have known when you refused the other constellations' sponsorship!]
Bihyung laughed like that for a long while before speaking again.
[I don't know how you learned about Star Stream broadcasting, but I can't accept that proposal. I'm a dokkaebi, not a constellation, so I can't become your constellation sponsor.]
“You seem to have misunderstood me. I never asked you to ‘sponsor’ me.”
[Pardon?]
“I know perfectly well that you're a weakling of a dokkaebi. I don't need your power. I need your ‘channel.’”
[My channel?]
“Judging by how little you understand, your Korean language patch must be incomplete.”
[Now, listen here.]
“I'll put it simply. I want to sign an exclusive contract with your channel.”
Bihyung stared blankly for a moment before finally coming to his senses.
[Wait. Are you saying you want to enter into a <Stream Contract> with me?]
“Yes.”
Stream contracts were originally agreements made between dokkaebis and constellations.
The constellations had their incarnations appear on a particular channel, and the dokkaebi took a portion of the coins those incarnations earned as a fee.
Normally, then, there was no room for the incarnation to take part in this agreement. They called it sponsorship, but a contracted incarnation was practically their sponsor's slave.
[Haha, this is something else.]
Bihyung laughed, covering his eyes with his tiny fingers. The air around us was changing.
[I don't know what you heard or where you heard it, but a human dares to mention a <Stream Contract>? And a worthless little insect without even a constellation sponsor, at that?]

Only his tone had changed, yet the air filled with murderous intent. As expected, even a low-ranking dokkaebi was incomparably stronger than a human. But if I were going to back down over something like that, I wouldn't have brought it up.
“It's because I don't have a constellation sponsor that I'm worth making a contract with.”
“Why do you think constellations come into channels?”
At the sudden question, Bihyung opened and closed his mouth like a dim-witted student. So it was time for a special lecture for a low-ranking dokkaebi.
“No need to be so nervous. You already know all this. But let's go over it once more as a review.”
Already drawn into my rhythm, Bihyung nodded without realizing it.

“The Star Stream's subscriber constellations (購讀座) can broadly be divided into two groups. One is the ‘entertainment seekers,’ who switch between channels to relieve their boredom. The other is the ‘incarnation seekers,’ who want to find incarnations to contract with. Right?”
[Yes. That's right.]

“That's why, to become a famous channel in the Star Stream, you have to be able to satisfy at least one of those groups. Put simply, you either focus on entertainment or find promising candidates for sponsorship. You have to do one of those two things properly.”
[You're quite knowledgeable. But so what? What do the constellations' reasons for subscribing have to do with this contract?]
“I've given you this much of a hint, and you still don't get it. That's why your subscriber count still hasn't made it past three digits.”
[······Shut up. Will you hurry up and tell me?]

As Bihyung pointed his little horn at me, there was something so adorable about him that it was hard to believe this was the dokkaebi who had been killing people by bursting their heads only a short while ago.
Enough teasing. Time to broach the subject.
“What if there were a channel that could satisfy both the ‘entertainment seekers’ and the ‘incarnation seekers’ at once?”
[What nonsense are you spouting? That's impossible. Even if it were possible, it would only last a little while.]
In fact, Bihyung was right.
The reason it was impossible to satisfy all the constellations lay in the nature of the ‘incarnation seekers.’
Constellations interested only in ‘seeking incarnations’ would quickly change channels once <Sponsor Selection> ended, however interesting an incarnation might be.
Thus, the ‘incarnation seekers’ were only ever temporary, one-off customers. But.
“That's assuming <Sponsor Selection> proceeds normally.”
[What?]
“What if there were an incarnation who never made a contract with any constellation? And what if that incarnation demonstrated abilities surpassing every other incarnation with a sponsor?”
A powerful incarnation attracted the constellations' attention simply by existing.
And if that incarnation continued to refrain from choosing a sponsor, the ‘incarnation seekers’ would naturally stay subscribed instead of leaving the channel.
[W-wait! Don't tell me that's why you didn't choose a sponsor······?]
“Yes, that's right.”
[Ha······ This is certainly interesting.]
Bihyung threw his head back and laughed, seemingly incredulous.

[The strongest incarnation, without a constellation sponsor······ If such a thing could exist, becoming the Star Stream's greatest channel certainly wouldn't be just a dream. But an incarnation like that can't exist.]
“Do you really think so?”

[······I'll admit you're no ordinary human. You've drawn quite a bit of attention from the constellations right from the start, and I've made a tidy profit thanks to you. But there's a limit to delusions. Even after what just happened,
you still haven't come to your senses? An ordinary human can never beat an incarnation with a constellation sponsor. That's the law of this world.]
“You don't know that.”

[You've already missed your chance. Look at yourself. You failed a mere sub-scenario, not even a main scenario, and now your life is in danger. There's no constellation anywhere who would want someone like you now―]
“Are you sure there isn't?”
“The constellations must be going wild by now. Aren't they? Aren't they all clamoring for you to hurry up and open the channel?”
Bihyung said nothing.

“They must be dying of curiosity by now. Who on earth is that lunatic challenging the ‘regressor’? Is he really a ‘prophet’? Can he actually see the future? And if he can, what on earth was he thinking, letting himself get eaten by an ichthyosaur?”
[S-stop! What on earth are you······.]
“That's what I'm about to show them. So just shut up and do as I say. I told you I'd make you the Dokkaebi King, didn't I?”
The look in Bihyung's eyes as he watched me was changing. His gulp was loud enough for even me to hear.
Bihyung was weighing it up.
He had nothing to lose by trusting me here, anyway. In that case?
Bihyung's eyes darted about.
[F-first, let's settle the penalty for failing the scenario. If you give me 5100 coins to start with······.]
“What are you talking about? I haven't failed.”
“The conditions should have been met by now······.”
I stretch and get to my feet. With a series of cracks, my body, growing stiff with cold, screamed in protest.
Bihyung still wore a dumbfounded expression.
“Just open the channel. It'll start soon.”
[Start? What on earth is―]
Then a message sounded from the air.
[A hidden scenario has arrived!]
<Hidden Scenario ― Commander Slayer>
Category: Hidden
Difficulty: A+
Clear conditions: Kill the ichthyosaur ‘Sea-Commander’ and escape from its belly.
Time limit: 10 days
Reward: 9000 coins
Failure: Death
“See? I told you to get ready, didn't I?”
There were three types of scenarios in Ways of Survival.
Main scenarios, which advanced the main story.
Sub-scenarios, which handled minor events.
And hidden scenarios, which unlocked only when special conditions were met.
[How on earth······?]
Bihyung's lips, twisted in astonishment, were trembling.
Unlike main scenarios and sub-scenarios, which were overseen by dokkaebis, hidden scenarios activated automatically when particular conditions were met.
“I suppose you wouldn't have known. You're a low-ranking dokkaebi.”
[What··· are you?]
“Anyway, if I clear this, I think that'll be more than enough to prove I have what it takes to make a contract. Don't you?”
For some reason, Bihyung glared at the scenario screen with gloomy eyes. Then he looked me over with concern and asked.
[This scenario's difficulty is A+. Do you really believe you can clear it?]
“Yes.”
Water from the Han River struck the ichthyosaur's stomach walls, raising small waves. Bihyung spoke again as the ripples subsided.
[······Fine. If you succeed in clearing this scenario, I'll agree to the contract.]
“We'll negotiate the terms after I clear the scenario.”
[Arrogant little······ I'll reopen the channel, then. Let's see you give it your best shot.]
“Oh, wait.”
He couldn't leave yet. There was something I absolutely had to check.
“There's still something you need to do.”
[······What now?]
Bihyung sounded somewhat put out.
“Fix the system error I'm experiencing.”
[A system error?]
“My Attributes Window won't open.”
[How could that be? The system can't have errors. The scenario system is perfection itself.]
“Take a look before you say that.”
Bihyung gave me a suspicious look, then began muttering something into the air.
[The dokkaebi ‘Bihyung’ is attempting ‘System Interference’ on you.]
System Interference.
An absolute interference skill usable only by dokkaebis with authority to interfere in scenarios.
In truth, it was unclear whether an error was the reason I couldn't view my ‘Attributes Window.’
But a dokkaebi, at least, should be able to discover something. And even if he couldn't, that would tell me something in its own right.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates!]
The next moment, sparks flew through the air, and Bihyung recoiled in shock.
Seeing how things were going, I had a rough idea of what was happening this time, too.
“What's wrong? Something not working?”
[This can't be. There can't be a protective barrier capable of blocking System Interference······?]
Apparently, the ‘Fourth Wall’ blocked interference not only from fellow incarnations, but from dokkaebis as well.
If that was true, it meant there was no one in ‘Ways of Survival,’ myself included, who could see my Attributes Window.
Interesting.
The perfect conditions for becoming a con artist.
“If you can't do it, forget it.”
[W-wait! I can do it. U-urgh. This, so, what if I do it like this?]
“I said, if you can't do it, forget it.”
[Gwaaaaaaah!]
He must have touched something he shouldn't have, because Bihyung began screaming wildly as though he were being electrocuted. The soft white fur on his skin was burning black.
[Th-this! This!]
“Enough. If it won't work, give up and do me another favor.”
[I can't! I am the dokkaebi Bihyung. On my honor as a dokkaebi, unless I resolve this situation―]
I checked the time. It had already been an hour since the ichthyosaur swallowed me. I had no time to waste like this.
“Dokkaebi Bag.”
Bihyung paused in his futile efforts in the air.
[What did you say?]
“Open the Dokkaebi Bag.”
[······How do you know about that, too?]
“Are you going to open it or not?”
[An incarnation without a constellation sponsor can't use the Dokkaebi Bag······.]
“Every incarnation who uses the Dokkaebi Bag has a constellation sponsor. But there's no rule saying an incarnation without a sponsor can't use it.”
[···Wait a moment.]
Bihyung took a manual out of his clothes and checked it, then remained silent for a long while.
[At this point, I don't know whether you're the dokkaebi or I am. Are you actually a dokkaebi?]
With an incredulous snort, Bihyung raised both hands.
[···Fine, there's no problem with you using it. But under the stream regulations, the Dokkaebi Bag can only be opened while the channel is open. Is that all right?]
“That's fine.”
[Channel #BI-7623 has opened.]
[The constellations are entering.]
A dazzling surge of electricity swept through the air. Soon, a transparent screen appeared before my eyes.
[Welcome to the coin shop, ‘Dokkaebi Bag.’]
Dokkaebi Bag.
It was the moment this goddamn world's ‘cash shop’ opened.
In the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ coins had two main uses.
One was to raise the levels of overall stats, including Constitution and Strength.
The other was to serve as a common currency for various shops, including the ‘Dokkaebi Bag.’
[Buy now! A starter package for your novice incarnation, just 2500 coins!]
[Special offer, today only! Get ahead of the competition with the 300% Growth Package!]
[Accidentally chose an incarnation with a lousy attribute? Don't worry! The ‘Random Attribute Box,’ which randomly changes attributes, is now available!]
Countless coin items, including all manner of packages.
The advertisements in the [Dokkaebi Bag] were all aimed at constellations raising incarnations.
Of course they were. The Dokkaebi Bag's customers were originally constellations.
I closed the advertising windows appearing like pop-ups, one by one.

Compared with the ‘disasters’ that appeared after the fifth main scenario, it was nothing, but an ichthyosaur of the ‘Sea Commander’ class was practically a catastrophe for incarnations in the early scenarios.
To kill the ichthyosaur, I absolutely needed certain items sold in the Bag.
Let's see······.
After flipping through the catalog for a long while, I glanced at Bihyung.
“Hey, are these the only products available right now? There should be a search function.”
[Oh, that's······ Damn it. Wait. Constellations-nim. Please. Calm down.]
Ever since the channel reopened, Bihyung had been sweating buckets like a cartoon character and pleading over and over.
[The broadcast only went down for a moment because of a server error! I didn't turn it off on purpose, I swear!]
There were about 20 stars twinkling above Bihyung's head at the moment.
Judging by how few constellations had left, quite a few seemed to want to see me as I was now.
Of course, not all the constellations were simply well-disposed toward me.
[A few constellations question the fairness of the broadcast!]
[A few constellations suspect preferential treatment!]
It wasn't something I hadn't anticipated.
A hidden scenario had actually begun during the brief interruption, and even the [Dokkaebi Bag] was open. It would have been stranger if the constellations weren't surprised.

[What do you mean, preferential treatment? Listen, Constellations-nim. I'm a dokkaebi. Don't you know I'd be annihilated immediately if I did something like that? You must know very well that the Storyteller's Oath is no trifling matter.]
“How about helping me first?”
[······The product search button is down there on the right.]
“Thanks.”
Leaving the flustered Bihyung to his troubles, I pressed the magnifying-glass icon hidden at the bottom of the package window.
[The product search function has been activated.]
[Product searches are limited to 5 per day. Each additional search costs 100 coins.]
Humans or dokkaebis, their sales tactics were all the same.
Five searches in total.
Two searches would be enough to buy the materials I needed, leaving me three.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is curious about your strategy.]
Yes, I bet you are.
If you're curious, watch closely.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ looks upon your every action with displeasure.]
If you don't like it, don't watch.
I spoke toward the search window.
“Product search: ‘Ancient Dragon.’”
[There are 3 search results.]
A small pop-up window appeared a moment later.
●Ancient Dragon's Heart - Stock ?
●Ancient Dragon's Bone - Stock 1
●Ancient Dragon's Horn - Stock 1
I selected ‘Ancient Dragon's Heart.’
<Item Information>
Name: Ancient Dragon's Heart
Grade: SS
Description: A heart containing the magic power of the ancient dragon ‘Ignitus.’ It holds nearly infinite magic power, and a successful heart transplant grants the elemental property ‘Hellfire.’
Price: 1500000 C
Stock: Just sold out.
So this was sold out, as expected.
Beyond the catalog, Bihyung, who had been dealing with the constellations, was staring at me with his chin thrust out.
[This is insane. How do you know about the ‘Ancient Dragon’?]
“I just tried a random name that sounded cool.”
[······That sounds like a lie.]
I shrugged.
Even in the original ‘Ways of Survival,’ the owner of the ‘Ancient Dragon's Heart’ had already been decided. If I remembered correctly, the owner of that heart was in Italy right now.
Lucky bastard. To land a constellation sponsor with a diamond spoon in their mouth.
I tried calling out a few more product names.
[The search for related products is complete.]
●Great Demon's Eyes - Stock 0
●White Pure Star Energy (白淸罡氣) - Stock 1
Even the ‘Great Demon's Eyes’ was sold out······ The constellations really were quick off the mark. Not that I could have bought it even if it were in stock, with its price of 1 million coins.
Having a sponsor really was nice.
The incarnation who obtained the ‘Great Demon's Eyes’ would now grow while smashing through every early scenario.
[What are you, really? You're not using some kind of cheat, are you? How do you know about items that can only be found through searches?]
“I told you, I just tried names that sounded plausible.”
In the end, of the three items I had searched for first, only ‘White Pure Star Energy’ remained in stock. Even that cost 10000 coins, so I couldn't buy it yet. Into the cart for now.
[What, you're not buying it?]
“I can't buy it right now anyway. I was just browsing.”
[Tch, then I opened this for nothing.]
“I'll buy something else instead, so bring up the items I name from now on.”
I called out a few item names. A moment later, an item list appeared before my eyes.
●Mucus of the Hammer Seahorse - Stock 124
●Stone Hog's Pointed Thorn - Stock 17

I finished comparing it with the list in my memory. The hammer seahorse, a sea monster species preyed upon (被食) by ichthyosaurs, and the stone hog, a natural enemy of sea monsters... No doubt about it. For taking down an ichthyosaur, this combination offered the best value for money.
“Four units of mucus and four spines. 800 coins should cover it, right?”
[It will, but······ these are junk items. What are you going to use them for?]
“You don't need to know.”

[······Not that I'm interfering, but why not buy something else? Say, <Moon Shadow Swordsmanship>. It's normally 8000 coins, but if you buy it now, I'll sell it for 4000. Buying that would probably help you clear the scenario more, wouldn't it?]
“Thanks, but I'll just buy these.”
Bihyung seemed displeased, but soon processed the payment.
[800 coins have been spent.]
Something like sparkling dust gathered in the darkness, and four long spines and four sacs filled with black mucus appeared.
[No refunds if you regret it now. You know that, right?]
“I know.”
After a brief nod, I got to work. I took off my shirt and tied it up, tucked the spines into the gaps, and hung the sacs at my waist.
Stone hog spines were blunt at the base but grew sharper toward the tip. They were roughly 1 meter long. A suitable size for piercing something.
[Hmm······ I'll be going, then. I can't stay glued to you alone. Some pretty interesting things are happening over there, too.]
“Go ahead.”
[Hehe, give it your best shot, then. May the story's blessing be with you.]
Once the glowing Bihyung disappeared, my surroundings grew dim again. I could have used my smartphone's light, but I needed to conserve its battery if possible.
The stone hog spines gave off a bluish glow in the darkness. Faint though it was, I would have to live by that light for a while.
I drew a spine from my waist and tried swinging it this way and that.
Perhaps because I didn't have a single proficiency skill like [Weapons Training] or [Incarnation of All Weapons], the spine stubbornly refused to feel natural in my hand.
[A few constellations are growing bored.]
It was about time for the impatient constellations to start leaving the channel. I couldn't see him here, but Bihyung might be getting anxious, too.
Another hour passed.
Right, left, up, down.
I wasn't entirely satisfied, but I no longer had trouble handling the spine. The surface was rough, so the spine didn't seem likely to slip easily from my hand, either.
Time to get started.
Putting a moderate amount of force behind it, I tried stabbing the ichthyosaur's stomach wall.
Twang!

The spine bounced straight back as though I had jabbed a highly elastic rubber wall. As expected, the ichthyosaur's stomach wasn't soft enough for me to tear through at my Strength level. It would probably be the same even if I used a skill.
Rrrrrumble.
That was when the little holes high on the stomach walls all opened at once.
A nauseating liquid spewing out with a gurgling sound.
“Gweeehk!”
A demonic human surrounded by the debris floating in the stomach began to shriek.
The demonic human's skin beginning to burn with a hissing sound.
The ichthyosaur had begun digesting.
The ichthyosaur's digestive fluid quickly dissolved into the river water, melting the concrete and debris and beginning to eat away at the surface beneath my feet.
Hissss!
No time left now.
Straight ahead as planned.
I leaped high off the floating debris and caught a protrusion on the stomach wall. Then I climbed the wall one handhold at a time, as though scaling a rock face.
Gush, gush, gush.
A digestive-fluid outlet was directly above me. Holding the spine between my teeth, I untied a mucus sac with my hand.
Mucus of the Hammer Seahorse.
I dipped my hand into the dark blue liquid with its dubious smell and carefully coated the spine with hammer seahorse mucus, starting at the tip.
Thoroughly and meticulously, like applying shaving cream to the area I was about to shave. Just as shaving cream protected skin from a razor, this mucus would protect the spine from digestive fluid.
Here goes.
I swung the spine toward the digestive-fluid outlet. The angle was precise, and I put every bit of strength I could currently muster into it.
Thuuunk!
The digestive fluid striking the spine splashed up and dissolved the skin on my forearm. Terrible pain hit me, but I didn't stop. One mistake here, and everything would be over.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ partially alleviates your pain.]
Gush-gush, gush, trickle. Dribble······.
At last, the spine firmly plugged the outlet.
“That's one.”
Barely managing to catch my breath, I drew another spine from my waist. Again, I coated it with hammer seahorse mucus, found another outlet, and blocked it.
[A few constellations admire your composure.]
[The constellations have donated 200 coins.]
Working steadily like that, I plugged three outlets. A few outlets remained, but their openings were small, so they didn't release much digestive fluid.
Catching my breath, I tightly wrapped and tied my shirt around an embedded spine. Now I had one spine and two mucus sacs left.
I spread the remaining mucus over my skin and clothes, then poured everything that was still left down my throat.
“Urgh.”
The salty, fishy taste lingered on my tongue, but it was better than dying. Compared with the catastrophe to come, this little bitter mouthful was nothing.
About 5 minutes later, the entire stomach began to shake with tremendous intensity.
······Has it started?
Kieeeeeeeee―!
The ichthyosaur's agonized scream. Blood vessels bulged between the writhing folds of the stomach wall. Spines burrowing between those vessels, extending their reach.
The spines lodged in the outlets had begun growing aggressively.
Stone hog spines grew in response to the bodily fluids of sea monsters.
Creak, cr-rack.
Made immune to digestive fluid by the coating of mucus, the spines absorbed the surrounding bodily fluids and began putting down roots in earnest inside the ichthyosaur's body.
The stone hog spines wouldn't stop spreading until the ichthyosaur was completely dead.
Kieeeeeee―!
Looking down at the corrosive liquid swirling beneath my feet, I gripped the spine tightly.
I had done everything I could. From now on, it was a battle of willpower.
Whether I died or this thing died.
Only one of us would survive.
I couldn't tell how much time had passed. My breathing frequently cut off, and every muscle in my body had grown so rigid that it would barely obey me.
[A few constellations admire your ability to survive!]
[The constellations have donated 100 coins.]

But I held on. I held on because I believed I could hold on. Watching the light emitted by the spine in the darkness reassured me that I was alive, and feeling the stomach wall's falling temperature convinced me that the creature was dying.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ admires your tenacity.]
[The constellation has donated 100 coins.]
When I grew hungry, I touched my tongue to the concentrated fluid beading at the spine's tip.

The concentrated fluid it secreted contained the life force drawn from throughout the ichthyosaur's body. I had swallowed the seahorse mucus beforehand so I could absorb this concentrated fluid without ill effects.
[Absorbing the ichthyosaur's power slightly increases your Constitution.]
The effect wasn't enough to raise the stat's level right away, but by the time I escaped the ichthyosaur, my Constitution would probably have risen by at least 2 levels.
It wouldn't work at higher levels, but it was one of the few tricks for raising Constitution without spending coins.
······This really isn't a dream, is it?
Was this really something I could do?
I'm just an ordinary reader.
I'm not the protagonist.
I felt as though I might wake up screaming under my covers at any moment, but no matter how often I blinked, no such miracle occurred.
······Would my mother be all right?
She would be. She was that ‘mother,’ after all, not just anyone.
Whenever the corrosive liquid pooled below drained away, I briefly fell asleep, and whenever cold river water flowed in through the ichthyosaur's mouth, I woke again.
Finally, the ichthyosaur stopped digesting. The warmth of the innards against my back rapidly cooled, and the once-elastic stomach grew steadily rigid. So I could be certain.
It was dead.
[······Truly remarkable.]
A brilliant surge of electricity through the darkness. Bihyung floated in the air, maintaining a hazy form.
[Using stone hog spines like that. It never even occurred to me. Wouldn't you agree, Constellations-nim?]
Bihyung spoke as he looked at the faintly glowing stone hog spines.

[Stone hogs mainly inhabit coastlines and prey on small sea monsters. They root their spines in their prey's skin and drain them dry, but to think he'd drive them into the digestive-fluid outlets······.]
Bihyung's brightly gleaming eyes weren't looking at me.
So those explanations weren't meant for me, either.
[A very few constellations smile in satisfaction as though they knew all along.]
[The constellations have donated 100 coins.]
[A few constellations belatedly understand your judgment.]
[The constellations complain that you should explain such things by talking to yourself next time.]
Ignoring the constellations' messages, I collected and drank the last of the concentrated fluid.
[Absorbing the ichthyosaur's power slightly increases your Constitution.]
[Your Constitution level has increased!]
[Constitution Lv.11 -> Constitution Lv.12]
With that, I had achieved my intended goal.
Bihyung descended beside me and continued speaking as he touched my blackened arm.
[And this mucus······ Even I didn't know the mucus of a hammer seahorse, a species preyed upon by ichthyosaurs, had this effect.]
Normally, the skin should have dissolved in the ichthyosaur's digestive fluid. I spoke in Bihyung's place.
“Hammer seahorse mucus is immune to digestive fluid. Since they're often eaten by ichthyosaurs, they apparently evolved that way.”
[A few constellations admire your extensive knowledge.]
Bihyung looked at me as though he'd taken a blow to the back of the head.
[Um, the explanations are my job······.]
“You didn't know much about it, so I did it for you. We're done with the explanations now, right?”
“Then give me my reward.”
[Damn bastard.]
As Bihyung grumbled, reward messages filled my vision.
[The hidden scenario has ended.]
[You have received 9000 coins as a reward.]
[You are the first to successfully hunt a grade 7 sea monster.]
[You have received 1000 coins as an achievement reward.
An extra 1000 coins on top of 9000. A very tidy haul.
[Coins held: 14800 C]
Including the extra 500 coins I earned by starring in a survival story I'd never expected to be part of, my total earnings came to 10500 coins. I had far exceeded my target.
[Haha, Constellations-nim. Did you enjoy the show? We'll get straight into the next scenario after a short advertisement!]
With those words, the faint sound of an advertisement came from somewhere.
A special package celebrating the launch of a new scenario, just 8800 coins······.
While the constellations' gazes were absent, Bihyung descended beside me and spoke in a friendly manner.
[Whew······ That was quite a survival story. The constellations' reactions were incredible, too.]
“How much time has passed?”
[Four days. I was on edge the whole time I watched. You didn't even know how long it had been?]
“My smartphone's battery died.”

It had taken far longer than I'd expected. My original goal had been two days······ Still, even Yoo Joonghyuk in his fourth round had taken four days to kill this thing, so I hadn't been particularly slow.
Anyway, I'd done it.
A pleasant sense of fulfillment spread through my body, bringing confidence with it. I was an ordinary person with ordinary abilities. But that didn't mean I could only do ordinary things.
It was a strange thing. Fiction that had never once helped me in 28 years was making someone as ordinary as me extraordinary.
[Oh, you're already talking to yourself?]
[You're pretty good, aren't you? Talking to yourself is a must for a proper incarnation. Of course, some constellations dislike it for being contrived, but usually······.]
“Quiet. Just open the Dokkaebi Bag.”
[Why? Got something to buy?]
“Something to buy and something to sell.”
[Damn it, then I'll have to turn down the ad for a moment. Constellations-nim, just a moment. I'll adjust the volume.]
While Bihyung opened the Dokkaebi Bag, I examined the spines embedded in the wall.
As the stomach wall hardened, deep cracks had formed around the spines. The weakened wall was now fragile enough for even my strength to smash through.
Using my one remaining spine, I broke through the wall and advanced little by little.
Before long, I came upon the ichthyosaur's core, shining a brilliant blue.
[Ichthyosaur's Core]
It was an ether core, found in monster species of grade 7 or higher. A precious item that, when processed and consumed, could raise one's Magic Power level without coins.
Perhaps because this was a Sea-Commander-class ichthyosaur, the core was in good condition, too.
After carefully cutting away the flesh surrounding the core, I emerged, and Bihyung stared at me in disbelief.
“I'll sell this.”
[You really······.]
“Of course, I don't mean I'll sell it to you. Put it up at the Dokkaebi Auction.”
Perhaps Bihyung was tired of asking me questions, because he seemed to decide to simply accept it.
[Whew······ Do as you like. So how much are you listing it for?]
“I'm not selling it for coins. I'll barter it.”
[Damn it, you know everything.]
Despite his grumbling, Bihyung uploaded the item to the Dokkaebi Auction. Perhaps because his desires were simple, he was more obedient than I'd expected.
“Someone will offer to buy it soon. And make sure the item I get in exchange is ‘Broken Faith.’”
[Broken Faith? I wonder if anyone has that······ Anyway, I've listed it.]
“Good. And what I want to buy······.”

I looked at the [White Pure Star Energy] in my cart. As expected, no one had bought it yet. Most constellations didn't know which coin items offered good value for money. Even though items from the ‘Dokkaebi Bag,’ with its aggressive pressure to spend, weren't necessarily good just because they were expensive.
[Wait, how about we talk for a moment before that?]
At Bihyung's words, the lowered advertisement volume rose again.
[The constellations complain about the prolonged advertisement.]
Watching an advertisement that had already played begin again, I had an instinctive sense of what Bihyung would say.
“Is this about the contract?”
Advertisements were the only way to block the constellations' eyes and ears without turning off the broadcast. It wouldn't do for them to hear what came next.
[Yes. I wasn't sure before, but watching this scenario gave me a little confidence. Well······ let's give it a try. If need be, I can help you a little along the way.]
“Wouldn't that violate the Storyteller's Oath?”
[Oh, of course I can't actually help you. It's just a figure of speech. Anyway, you're going to sign, right?]
“What are the terms?”
[Read it.]
It seemed he'd even prepared a fancy contract, being a dokkaebi and all.
I began reading the contract that appeared in the air as a transparent window.
<Stream Contract Agreement>
1. Incarnation Kim Dokja (Party A) shall be bound by an exclusive contract with dokkaebi Bihyung (Party B) until all scenarios have ended or Party A dies.
“······I'm Party A?”
[Haha, humans like that sort of thing, don't they? It doesn't mean anything anyway. Go on, keep reading.]
1. Incarnation Kim Dokja (Party A) shall never select a constellation sponsor until all scenarios have ended or Party A dies.
I had expected this, too.
1. Incarnation Kim Dokja (Party A) shall operate exclusively on the channel of dokkaebi Bihyung (Party B).
2. Incarnation Kim Dokja (Party A) and dokkaebi Bihyung (Party B) shall share the revenue earned through the stream contract in a ratio determined by mutual agreement.
1. Incarnation Kim Dokja (Party A) and dokkaebi Bihyung (Party B) shall, upon violating this contract, be sentenced to annihilation under the laws of the <Star Stream>.
I read the contract carefully through the final clause. I had thought he'd try something underhanded, assuming I didn't know any better, but I couldn't see anything like that.
Except for one thing.
“An important part is missing, though.”
[You mean the seal? You just have to say you agree. A stream contract is a soul oath, so―]
“I'm talking about the ratio.”
[Oh, ah. Haha. Right.]
The bastard was playing dumb.
That was the most important part.

[How about 5:5? In exchange, I'll waive your channel fees. Oh, you know how it's calculated, right? We'll split the donations you receive from now on according to that exact ratio. For example, if you receive 100 coins, you keep 50 and I keep 50.]

Every <Stream Contract> worked like this. Constellations put their incarnations on a dokkaebi's channel, then split the donations received from other constellations according to an agreed ratio. Normally, that was how it went.
“Do you take me for a sucker? No deal.”
[What? B-but this is the standard revenue split in the industry······.]

“I'm an incarnation without a constellation sponsor. And when constellations donate to an incarnation without a sponsor, they have to pay the dokkaebi an enormous fee. You must have already made quite a profit thanks to me.”
Bihyung's jaw slowly dropped. But making that face wouldn't help him now.
“10:0. You can get by on the fees alone. I'm not paying you a penny.”
[What?! That's ridiculous······ How about 7, 7:3?]
My share shot up in an instant. But I wasn't making any concessions.
[What the fuck is this bullshit! A ridiculous split like that―]
“If you don't like it, forget it. I'll just go to another channel. ‘Gildal’ is doing pretty well these days, so I'll have to ask Gildal.”
[······8:2. I can't give you any more than that.]

Bihyung's expression turned threatening. An oppressive force bore down on me, as though he might burst my head at any moment. But I knew. He could never give up on this contract. My existence would be his last chance.
“The ad's about to end. Can't you see the constellations complaining?”
At last, Bihyung raised both hands as though giving up.
[Goddamn it, fine. You'll sign the contract, then?]
He was surrendering more easily than I'd expected.
I had actually intended to compromise at around 9:1.
······Maybe he was pocketing even more money on the side than I knew. Somehow, that pissed me off.
“Yes. And one more thing.”
[What? There's more?]
“You need to pay a separate signing bonus, don't you? Hand over 5000 coins.”
For a moment, Bihyung's expression went blank.
[······Y-you really.]
I grinned.
Why ‘Party A’ held the upper hand, why humans clung so fiercely to that supposedly meaningless position······ I'd teach you myself, you damned dokkaebi.
[The stream contract has been concluded.]
[You have received 5000 coins as a signing bonus.]
Soon, the advertisement ended and the constellations returned. Patting the dokkaebi on the shoulder, I spoke.
“Well, shall we head outside?”
This is where it really begins.
